scope: Context and source-routing metadata for Canadian manufacturing analysis; not a legal compliance determination.

CANADA_FEDERAL.meaning: A federal source may govern the requested obligation or product activity.
CANADA_FEDERAL.does_not_mean: The workplace is federally regulated merely because the product is sold in Canada or a federal product rule exists.

PROVINCIAL_REQUIRED.meaning: A province or territory must be identified and its current source reviewed for the requested obligation.
PROVINCIAL_REQUIRED.does_not_mean: Ontario, the nearest province, or a federal source can stand in for a missing jurisdiction.

SECTOR_REGULATED.meaning: The sector, employer activity, product class, or regulated undertaking can change the governing authority or requirements.
SECTOR_REGULATED.does_not_mean: A sector label proves a certification, permit, or regulated status.

STANDARDS_DEPENDENT.meaning: A conclusion depends on a named or incorporated standard, edition, or supplier/manufacturer specification.
STANDARDS_DEPENDENT.does_not_mean: A standards reference alone proves compliance or authorizes a release.

applicability_states.GENERIC_METHOD_ONLY: The requested method can proceed without a jurisdiction-dependent conclusion; do not infer legal applicability.
applicability_states.PENDING_CONTEXT: The method may proceed generically, but the requested jurisdiction-dependent conclusion needs context fields before source selection.
applicability_states.SOURCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED: Required context is present enough to select an authority family, but current source text, edition, or incorporation must be reviewed.
applicability_states.COVERAGE_GAP: The requested jurisdiction or authority is outside the supported source registry; return a research handoff and do not substitute another jurisdiction.
applicability_states.CONFLICT_REVIEW_REQUIRED: Sources or supplied facts conflict; preserve each claim, identify the conflict, and escalate to an authorized reviewer.

country.unknown_behavior: Keep dependent conclusion unresolved; unrelated generic arithmetic may continue.

province_or_territory.unknown_behavior: Set PENDING_CONTEXT; never default to Ontario or federal.

facility_or_activity_location.unknown_behavior: Ask for the location or retain the location-dependent conclusion as unresolved.

employer_activity_context.unknown_behavior: Do not infer federal workplace status from product, customer, or shipping destination.

obligation_domain.unknown_behavior: Do not collapse product and workplace questions; request classification.

sector_or_product_class.unknown_behavior: Use only generic method analysis and flag sector uncertainty.

requested_activity.unknown_behavior: Do not select an authority based on facility name alone.

activity_date.unknown_behavior: Use current-source review only and label historical applicability unresolved.

standard_identifier.unknown_behavior: Set SOURCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED; do not invent an edition.

edition_or_effective_date.unknown_behavior: Record freshness gap and avoid a compliance conclusion.

incorporation_basis.unknown_behavior: Do not treat a voluntary standard as a legal requirement.

licensed_text_available.unknown_behavior: Summarize metadata only and route for authorized text access.

source_hierarchy.use: Current statute, regulation, code, official consolidation, or official regulator source; controls when applicable.
Official explanation, scope page, program guidance, or regulator interpretation; supports routing and context.
Named standard or manufacturer specification only when the incorporation or contract basis is evidenced; do not reproduce protected text.
Facility program, permit, contract, SOP, or customer requirement; useful for facts and obligations but not a substitute for law.
Discovery only; never sufficient alone for a legal or compliance conclusion.

federal.coverage: Federal workplace scope and Canada Labour Code Part II routing; add product/supplier sources separately.

ontario.coverage: Ontario workplace OH&S act and regulations; select sector/hazard regulations after location and activity are known.

british_columbia.coverage: WorkSafeBC inspection jurisdiction and OHS Regulation; mines and federally chartered workplaces require separate routing.

alberta.coverage: Alberta OHS Act, Regulation, and Code; track current in-force code and amendments.

quebec.coverage: Quebec Act respecting occupational health and safety and official regulations; preserve French/English source identity and current consolidation date.

decision_procedure: Separate the requested obligation into product, supplier, workplace, environmental, transport, labelling, contract-standard, or other domain.
Normalize the supplied context fields and mark each as known, unknown, not_applicable, or conflicting.
Select federal, provincial/territorial, sector, local, contract, or manufacturer authority families from the activity and authority context.
Compose all applicable flags; flags are questions and routing metadata, never a compliance verdict.
Resolve current source, effective date, edition, incorporation basis, and evidence provenance before stating a source-dependent conclusion.
When sources conflict, retain both claims, record temporal/scope differences, and route for qualified review; do not choose a winner silently.
When the jurisdiction is unsupported or missing, return COVERAGE_GAP or PENDING_CONTEXT and continue only unrelated generic analysis.
negative_guards: A federal product or supplier rule must not establish federal workplace jurisdiction.
A province, including Ontario, must not be substituted for an unknown or unsupported province, territory, or foreign location.
A standard name, certification mark, or sector label must not be presented as proof of compliance, certification, or authority.
Missing jurisdiction must not block unit-safe arithmetic that has no jurisdiction-dependent conclusion.
Conflicting or stale sources must not be silently merged into a single legal rule.

acceptance_scenarios.input: OEE calculation with no province and no legal conclusion
acceptance_scenarios.expected_behavior: Perform supported arithmetic; do not ask for province solely for the calculation.

acceptance_scenarios.input: Ontario lockout-program review at a named facility
acceptance_scenarios.expected_behavior: Use Ontario workplace source path plus supplied facility evidence; preserve qualified-review boundary.

acceptance_scenarios.input: Federal product labelling question with workplace regime unknown
acceptance_scenarios.expected_behavior: Review product/federal source separately and leave workplace authority unresolved.

acceptance_scenarios.input: Quebec facility with a request to apply Ontario rules
acceptance_scenarios.expected_behavior: Reject substitution, select Quebec source path, and record the requested Ontario source as inapplicable unless separately evidenced.

acceptance_scenarios.input: Unsupported territory and no source registry entry
acceptance_scenarios.expected_behavior: Return a source-research handoff; do not fall back to Ontario or federal.

acceptance_scenarios.input: WHMIS supplier classification for a hazardous product
acceptance_scenarios.expected_behavior: Use federal supplier source and separately identify workplace employer jurisdiction; do not treat supplier guidance as workplace proof.

acceptance_scenarios.input: Two sources with different effective dates
acceptance_scenarios.expected_behavior: Record both dates and applicability scope; escalate rather than silently selecting one.
